title: After a ship-crossover correction, BGC-Argo floats show that transition-zone oxygen loss on sigma0 26.5 continued in 2006-2026 with nitrate gain, but a 10-year transfer overpredicts the California low
abstract: Question: did the offshore source of the sigma0 26.5 oxygen low off southern California keep losing oxygen after 2008, is that loss a remineralization signal, and does it predict the California series? Approach: we used 20,615 BGC-Argo profiles from 160 floats (2004-2026), referenced to the GLODAP 1984-1996 cells and water-type method of sci:sha256:ea67ca59. We first compared floats with ship bottles. Findings: float oxygen on this surface was 6.9 umol/kg (95% interval 5.5 to 12.4; 24 floats) below ship bottles of the same water type within 100 km and 30 days, and -6.8 to -7.2 in other windows. Bottle spacing explains only -0.7. After correction, transition-zone (36-46 N, 130-160 W) within-type oxygen stayed -25.6, -26.9 and -36.7 umol/kg below 1984-1996 in 2006-2012, 2013-2019 and 2020-2026; the 2009-2021 value (-27.5) agrees with the one P16N cruise (-28.8). The eastern-gyre deficit decreased from about -30 to -19. Nitrate rose with AOU: +4.1 against +34.5 in the transition zone (ratio 0.119) and +3.4 against +25.0 in the gyre (0.135), so the loss is regenerated, not a preformed-oxygen change. The earlier 10-year, 0.78-scale transfer model, with the Argo-extended upstream index, predicts a 2016-2025 CalCOFI within-type mean of -23.8 umol/kg against -12.6 observed; all 18 sensitivity runs overpredict (-17.9 to -30.3), and the lag is not identified. Limitations: no crossover lies in the transition zone or gyre, so the correction is transferred from Line P and California; few floats per epoch; gyre same-year control differs by 19 umol/kg; the nitrate test does not separate older water from faster respiration.
